issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: The problem statement contains contradictory directives. In one place (problem statement lines 70-74) it instructs students to make stock a final instance field initialized to a default value in the SealSaloon constructor (i.e., an instance-level final Stock set up in the constructor). Elsewhere (problem statement lines 77-81) it explicitly states that the stock attribute must be static (shared across all instances). The reference solution (SealSaloon.java line 5) declares stock as a private static final and initializes it at declaration. This conflict leaves students uncertain whether to declare stock as an instance final field and initialize it in the constructor or as a static final field initialized at declaration/static initializer, which affects both the correct declaration and initialization location.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended design explicit and consistent: state that SealSaloon.stock is a static final field (shared across all SealSaloon instances) and instruct students to initialize it either at the point of declaration or in a static initializer block. Update the UML and all textual references to mark 'stock' as static (e.g., +/static/final) and remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor. If the educational intent is to keep it instance-level, instead update the solution and all static-related notes to treat stock as a non-static final instance field initialized in the constructor.

issues.description: Field SealSaloon.totalOrders: The UML in the problem statement declares totalOrders as int (SealSaloon.-totalOrders: int) while the reference solution (SealSaloon.java line 6) declares totalOrders as a long (private long totalOrders = 0;). This mismatch between the specified type (int) and the implemented type (long) can confuse students about the expected type and whether to use int or long for the attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type consistent across specification and implementation. Either change the UML and textual description to specify 'long totalOrders' (preferred if anticipating large counts) or change the reference solution to use 'int totalOrders'. Update the problem text and UML to reflect the chosen type so students know which primitive to implement.
